conjecture: EJ = K·P_y, i.e. the segment EJ on the tangent g has the same length as the segment K P_y, which is parallel to j (numerically both ≈ 11.345).
reason: Numerical check: J lies on g, since J−E is parallel to C−E, and K P_y is parallel to j. Also |EJ| = |K P_y| ≈ 11.345. I did not derive this equality in general. The sketch below is the expected mechanism, not a proof. In right triangle F P_x P_y the right angle is at P_x. Since FP_x² = FV·FP_y, the point V is the foot-type point of the altitude relation, so V, P_x, P_y, K sit in similar-triangle position on the pencil of lines through F. Because P_x lies on h1, which is parallel to e and passes through V, the points K on e and P_y on m are tied together by this mean-proportional law. The length K P_y measured along the direction of j is then fixed by the data and does not depend on P_x. Constructing H on j and J on g with HJ ∥ GE transfers that length onto the tangent g. In that construction K P_y, which is parallel to j, and EJ, which lies on g, correspond under the symmetry of the two tangents from C and the reflection in line CA. This gives EJ = K P_y for every P_x.
